newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes up, borrowing boosts palladium.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes up, borrowing boosts palladium.

text.p: Precious metal prices were expected to move narrowly around opening levels on Tuesday as the markets re-gathered momentum after a holiday weekend in the United States and London.
Dealers said business had been very quiet on Monday in the Far East where a weaker yen encouraged some buying of gold on Tocom, but gave little further direction.
Gold was fixed at $343.55 per ounce up a dollar from Friday when London closed at $342.80/$343.30.
"There may be some activity later but range trading seems the order of the day," one dealer said.
In fact the early interst came in palladium were a large borrowing order set prices jangling.

Palladium quickly jumped about four dollars from its opening to $174.00/$175.00 and platinum, having firmed a couple of dollars from its $389.50/$390.50 opening, tried $395.00/$396.00 in the reaction.
"They are both trying to go higher," a dealer said.
Palladium was firmer in Tokyo earlier as dealers there began to see as overdone last week's selling reaction to news Russian exports would begin for the first time this year at end May, early June.

Also cited behind the firmer palladium futures price was the realisation that even if export negotiations began between Russia and the Japanese trade houses on schedule on June 1, it would be July before metal arrived to ease market tightness.
Russia, the largest exporter of palladium has not shipped any metal this year after local administrative problems delayed the start of export negotiations last December.
Spurred by the tightness of supply, palladium reached its second highest fixing on record last week at $180.50, a dollar below the highest set in 1989, the year official palladium fixings began.
Platinum's reaction to the borrowing, by a Japanese house according to dealers, took it to well established resistance between 395.00-$400.00.
Silver held on to $4.74/$4.76 which it attained on a short-covering rally late on Friday.
Dealers have been wary of silver recently on account of its volatility and the more obvious need to be involved in platinum and palladium.
